question: Surya Sen was associated with which of the following radical activities against British?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chittagong Armory Raid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Surya Sen, popularly known as Master Da, was a prominent Indian freedom fighter and the chief architect of the Chittagong Armory Raid.
 
• The Chittagong Armory Raid took place on 18 April 1930 in Chittagong, then part of British India (now in Bangladesh).
 
• Surya Sen led a group of revolutionaries in an attempt to raid the British armory in Chittagong and seize weapons to fight against the British rule.
 
• The raid was an important event in the history of Indian independence movement as it demonstrated the spirit and determination of Indian revolutionaries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kakori Conspiracy**

 
 
• The Kakori Conspiracy was an armed robbery on the Kakori train near Lucknow on 9 August 1925 by the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA).
 
• Prominent revolutionaries involved included Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan, and Chandrashekhar Azad.
 
• The objective was to fund their revolutionary activities by looting the government treasury carried in the train.
 
 
 
• **Muzaffarpur Conspiracy Case**
 
 
• This was an assassination attempt on the British official Kingsford by Indian revolutionaries Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki on 30 April 1908.
 
• The attack took place in Muzaffarpur, Bihar, but resulted in the death of two British women instead of Kingsford.
 
• Khudiram Bose was later arrested and executed, becoming a martyr in the Indian independence movement.
 
 
 
• **Delhi Conspiracy Case**
 
 
• This was a plot to assassinate the then Viceroy of India, Lord Hardinge, during a procession in Delhi on 23 December 1912.
 
• The attack was planned by Rash Behari Bose and Basanta Kumar Biswas, who threw a bomb at Lord Hardinge's elephant.
 
• Although Lord Hardinge was injured, he survived the attack.
 
 
 
• **Chittagong Armory Raid**
 
 
• The raid was an attempt by Indian revolutionaries to raid the armory of the police and auxiliary forces from the Chittagong armory on 18 April 1930.
 
• Surya Sen led a group of revolutionaries in this endeavor, with the aim of destroying the British control over the region.
 
• Although they were unable to achieve their ultimate goal, the raid inspired many and highlighted the bravery and commitment of the revolutionaries.
 
• Surya Sen was eventually captured and hanged by the British on 12 January 1934.
